clue.text: The weather forecast is good for the regularly held village show

definitions.meaning: a barometer pointer at this setting promises settled sunny weather
a fair held at fixed, established times each year in a village

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes a barometer reading promising fine weather and also an established fair held on a fixed schedule.

clue.text: Invite a whisky drinker to fix a date

definitions.meaning: the pourer asks the drinker to call a halt when the glass holds enough
to name the day or time something should happen

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is what a host says while pouring a drink, and also a request to nominate a convenient day.

clue.text: Close connection

definitions.meaning: as an adjective, finished or done with, as in 'we're done'
a telephone operator says this once a call has been put across to the other party

explanation.definitionFit: The word means finished, as at the close of something, and also describes being connected on a phone line.

clue.text: Feature of Hampton Court most likely to astonish

definitions.meaning: the famous hedge labyrinth in the palace gardens, read as two words with the article
to astound or stun

explanation.walkthrough: Hampton Court is a Tudor palace near London whose gardens hold a well-known hedge labyrinth; 'most likely to' is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Split as an article plus a puzzle of hedges, it names the palace's labyrinth; joined up it is a synonym of astound.

clue.text: Aide-memoire about a book in the sale

indicators.note: about means the first piece goes round the next one

parts.note: an aide-memoire is a reminder, something to jog the memory

explanation.surface: A memo concerning a discounted volume in a shop's sale.
explanation.definitionFit: Unsold copies of a book offered off cheaply by the publisher are called by this name.

clue.text: No wonder little light is shed on the east coast of ireland

definitions.text: No wonder little light is shed on the east coast of ireland

parts.words: No wonder little light is shed on the east coast of ireland
parts.note: read as a phrase, a lamp burning dimly because its burning cord is turned down; also the Irish county on that coast

explanation.walkthrough: Split it into two words: a lamp's burning cord turned right down sheds little light, and the whole is a county on Ireland's east coast, south of Dublin.
explanation.definitionFit: The county lies on Ireland's eastern seaboard, and split in two its name pictures a turned-down lamp.

clue.text: Fail to make good use of the environmental disposal problem

definitions.text: Fail to make good use of
definitions.meaning: to squander or fritter away
rubbish or refuse that has to be got rid of

explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means squander; as a noun it means rubbish needing disposal.

clue.text: MP most likely to lash out?

definitions.text: MP most likely to lash out?

parts.words: MP most likely to lash out?
parts.note: the parliamentary officer who enforces party discipline bears a title suggesting a lash

explanation.walkthrough: In the UK Parliament this senior party officer keeps members voting the party line; the title suggests a whip for lashing.
explanation.definitionFit: The senior party enforcer in Parliament is named after a lash, so is the member most likely to wield one.

clue.text: A loading vessel which has presumably, been unloaded

definitions.meaning: a flat-bottomed barge used to load and unload ships in harbour
having had its load removed, so weighing less

explanation.definitionFit: A harbour barge carrying cargo to and from ships has this name, and anything relieved of its cargo weighs less.

clue.text: Wheeled out to persuade by cajolery

indicators.note: out suggests the letters of the word wheeled are turned out of their order

explanation.surface: Someone wheeled out to sweet-talk others into agreeing.
explanation.definitionFit: To coax or flatter someone into doing something is a synonym phrase for cajoling.

clue.text: A section of the CID from which mutineers were suspended

indicators.note: of puts the section after the body it belongs to, so the second piece follows

parts.note: the CID, the Criminal Investigation Department, is associated with Scotland Yard
an arm is a section or branch of an organisation

explanation.surface: A branch of the detective department that dealt with mutinous sailors.
explanation.walkthrough: Scotland Yard is London's police headquarters; mutineers were traditionally hanged from the end of a ship's spar.
explanation.definitionFit: Mutineers were hanged from the end of the horizontal spar on a ship's mast.

clue.text: Bob seen on a gravelly beach

definitions.meaning: a short cropped hairstyle for women, popular in the 1920s
a shore covered with small rounded pebbles

explanation.definitionFit: The word names a short bobbed haircut and also a shore of loose pebbles.

clue.text: The good woman used to patch the soldiers' clothes

definitions.meaning: the woman who runs the home

definitions.text: used to patch the soldiers' clothes
definitions.meaning: a small sewing kit of needles and thread issued to soldiers for repairs

explanation.definitionFit: The word names a woman managing a home and also a soldier's pocket sewing kit, often pronounced 'hussif'.

clue.text: Sounds fated to be treated like a returninghero

indicators.note: sounds says the word that follows is heard rather than written, giving a different spelling

parts.note: these words are said aloud, and what is heard is the sound this part of the answer needs

explanation.surface: Someone doomed by destiny is welcomed back like a conquering champion.
explanation.definitionFit: A returning hero is celebrated with parties and honours, which is the synonym meant.

clue.text: The prophet with a human disposition

indicators.note: disposition, an arrangement, signals the letters of human are laid out afresh

explanation.surface: A holy seer with a kindly, humane temperament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disposition' looks like temperament but means rearrangement of HUMAN.
explanation.definitionFit: He is one of the minor prophets of the Old Testament, with a book named after him.

clue.text: Christie play in which doctor had to employ a pony carriage

parts.note: MO, medical officer, is a doctor
to employ is to use
a trap is a light two-wheeled carriage pulled by a pony

explanation.surface: A medic in an Agatha Christie drama has to hire a horse-drawn cart.
explanation.walkthrough: Agatha Christie's play has run in London's West End since 1952.
explanation.definitionFit: Agatha Christie wrote this long-running murder-mystery stage play.

clue.text: Black Beauty could be a turn up for the books?

definitions.meaning: the horse in Anna Sewell's novel has a black coat

definitions.text: a turn up for the books?
definitions.meaning: an unexpected winner who surprises the bookmakers

explanation.definitionFit: A black-coated steed fits literally, and an unfancied competitor who wins is a surprise to bookmakers.

clue.text: Maybe a MIG, the first of two to reach Mars

parts.note: a MiG fighter was a Soviet, or Red, aircraft

indicators.note: the first of means take only the opening letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A Soviet jet fighter is the first of a pair to fly to Mars.
explanation.definitionFit: The fourth planet is known by this nickname for its rusty colour.

clue.text: Squared up with a banker's draft before the account was overdrawn

indicators.note: before places the draft ahead of the overdrawn piece

parts.note: a draft written on a bank account is a cheque
an overdrawn account is said to be in the red

explanation.surface: Settling up with a bank draft just before the account went into debt.
explanation.definitionFit: A pattern of alternating squares, like a draughtboard, is described this way.

clue.text: Can a saint get on top of a card game?

indicators.note: in a down clue the earlier pieces sit above, on top of, the final letter

explanation.surface: A whimsical question whether a holy person can master a game of cards.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a rummy-type game played with two packs, popular in the mid-twentieth century.

clue.text: Soil one's lips with obsequious apologies?

definitions.text: Soil one's lips with obsequious apologies?

parts.words: Soil one's lips with obsequious apologies?
parts.note: a phrase for grovelling humiliation, read literally as putting earth in the mouth

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to humble oneself abjectly, which the clue renders literally as dirtying the mouth.

clue.text: The rest of the birds find fish

definitions.meaning: a bar or branch on which birds sit and rest
a spiny-finned freshwater fish

explanation.definitionFit: The word names a roost for birds and also a common freshwater fish.

clue.text: Take over duties from an old steward about 51

indicators.note: about means the steward's letters go round the number

parts.note: a reeve was a steward or manager of an estate in medieval England
LI is 51 in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Replacing a retired estate manager who is around fifty-one.
explanation.definitionFit: To stand in for someone at the end of their shift is a synonym for taking over.

clue.text: Slashes review but wrangles

indicators.note: review, a fresh look over, signals the letters of slashes are reorganised

explanation.surface: A critic savages a show, yet the arguments continue.
explanation.definitionFit: Squabbles and disputes are a synonym for annoying arguments of this kind.

clue.text: In bacon it reduces curing time

definitions.text: In bacon it reduces curing time

indicators.note: in says the letters sit inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A preserving agent that speeds up the curing of bacon.
explanation.definitionFit: Saltpetre, potassium nitrate, is used to cure bacon and speeds the process.

clue.text: Narrate "James and the Giant Peach"!

parts.note: to narrate a children's story is to recount stories; to peach is to inform on someone

explanation.walkthrough: Roald Dahl's book is a tale, but 'peach' also means to inform on someone, so the phrase also means to sneak.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means to recount stories and also to blab or inform, as 'peach' means.

clue.text: It upset a drunken spy-half drunk anyway

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means the word it is turned upside down, reading bottom to top
drunken signals the letters of spy reel about into a new order

explanation.surface: A drunken spy knocks things over while somewhat inebriated.
explanation.definitionFit: Slightly inebriated, merry rather than fully plastered, is the sense.

clue.text: It pulls many tourists to London

definitions.text: It pulls many tourists to London

parts.words: It pulls many tourists to London
parts.note: literally something that tows, and also the famous fortress by the Thames that draws visitors

explanation.walkthrough: The Tower of London is a major tourist attraction; read literally, the word is also one that tows.
explanation.definitionFit: London's historic fortress draws crowds of visitors, and one who tows is also named so.

clue.text: A rest for the feet when on the trot

definitions.text: A rest for the feet when on the trot

parts.words: A rest for the feet when on the trot
parts.note: the loop hanging from a saddle that supports a rider's foot

explanation.definitionFit: A rider's foot sits in this saddle loop while the horse trots.

clue.text: What Roosevelt called for when the cards were stacked against him

definitions.text: What Roosevelt called for when the cards were stacked against him

parts.words: What Roosevelt called for when the cards were stacked against him
parts.note: a card player wanting a fresh hand, and the US president's 1930s economic programme

explanation.walkthrough: Franklin D. Roosevelt's programme against the Great Depression is named like a card player's request for fresh cards.
explanation.definitionFit: Roosevelt's economic recovery programme carried this name, also what a losing card player asks for.

clue.text: Examining body

parts.note: reads like a board of examiners, but means the inspection of a corpse

explanation.definitionFit: A post-mortem is the examination of a corpse to find the cause of death.

clue.text: For English art collectors they're tops!

definitions.text: For English art collectors they're tops!

parts.words: For English art collectors they're tops!
parts.note: paintings by the English landscape artist J. M. W. Turner, and lathe workers who make spinning tops

explanation.walkthrough: J. M. W. Turner was a great English painter; workers at a lathe also make toy spinning tops.
explanation.definitionFit: Works by the painter Turner are prized by collectors, and lathe craftsmen turn wooden tops.
